newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rice export prices seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rice export prices seen mixed.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices are likely to remain mixed next week after the four-day Moslem Eid al-Adha festival, dealers said on Wednesday.
Export enquiries plunged before the festival, which starts on Thursday, exporter Khalid Ghori of Matco Rice Processing said. "Rice prices are almost stable compared to last week."
Ghori said a domestic wheat flour shortage had not pushed up rice export prices.

Howeve, one local rice dealer said retail prices for IRRI-6 rice had firmed slightly on extra buying stimulated by rising prices for wheat flour, which is in short supply partly because of smuggling to neighbouring countries.
Pakistan exported 1.207 million tonnes of rice worth $338 million in the first nine months of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) compared to 1.015 million tonnes worth $335 million in the year-ago period.
In March, rice exports fell to 188,502 tonnes worth $55 million compared to 207,191 tonnes worth $52 million in February and 186,760 tonnes worth $58 million in March 1996.
